page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7T83 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.55 GHz, this configuration provides 8 dedicated vCPUs spanning 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. System memory totals 16.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 2.0 GB of memory per core. The instance lacks local ephemeral storage and dedicated GPU accelerators, relying on remote block storage for disk operations. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 2 Gbps.

Performance testing highlights strong single-core execution alongside balanced multi-core throughput. In single-core stress-ng CPU benchmarks, the instance ranks in the top 25% of evaluated systems, supported by hardware acceleration for AES cryptography and bit manipulation instruction sets. Multi-core performance across stress-ng, Geekbench 5, and PassMark tests aligns with standard mid-tier results. Uncached memory write throughput measures 18.88 GB/sec, placing in the lower performance tier, whereas cached small-block read bandwidth reaches 516.94 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the resource profile prioritizes processing capabilities over memory capacity and local disk performance. Benchmark metrics show weaker processing speeds on medium LLM inference tasks (17.15 prompt tokens/sec), indicating limited suitability for compute-heavy AI model workloads. However, high single-core performance combined with steady Redis throughput of 8.09 million SET operations/sec makes this server well-matched for web serving, software compilation, CI/CD runners, and microservices.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server hosted on the KVM hypervisor. Driven by an AMD EPYC 7T83 x86_64 processor clocked at 2.55 GHz, it supplies 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading and 16.0 GB of system RAM. The instance features no local disk storage or GPU acceleration and offers a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks indicate strong single-threaded CPU execution in stress-ng tests, placing in the upper quartile, alongside middle-tier multi-threaded scoring across Geekbench and PassMark suites. Memory operations reveal a lower write throughput of 18.88 GB/sec, while static web serving and Redis key-value workloads maintain consistent mid-range output. This server profile is best suited for compute-focused tasks, CI/CD compilation pipelines, web application servers, and microservice hosts where local disk storage and large memory footprints are not required.
